title: Los Alamos–Battelle Nitinol contract of 1949
place_text: Los Alamos, New Mexico / Battelle Memorial Institute

tellings.quote: veterans of World War II. Some of the most interesting evidence I found for Roswell is actually that there was a contract between Los Alamos and Battelle Memorial Institute in 1949

related.note: Both are the 1949 Battelle contract that led to Nitinol and is offered as Roswell evidence. This telling makes Los Alamos the other party, where the story says Wright Field.

plain: In 1949 Los Alamos, the US nuclear weapons laboratory in New Mexico, signed a contract with the Battelle Memorial Institute, a private research institute, tied to work on Nitinol, a nickel and titanium metal that springs back to its original shape. Michels says this himself, without naming the document's wording, and calls it some of the most interesting evidence he has found for Roswell, the reported 1947 crash of an unknown craft in New Mexico, because shape-recovering metal is said to have been found in the debris.
